content.text: {"answer":"Medical knowledge graphs can support clinical LLMs by supplying structured knowledge, linking patient evidence to biomedical concepts, and making retrieved evidence traceable [1, 2, 5]. One study finds that KG-judgment training with KL regularization makes sparse model updates and can improve reasoning, while task-specific fine-tuning produces denser updates [1]. MM-KG explicitly connects multimodal patient observations with biomedical relations and retrieves relevant subgraphs for an LLM [2]. Other approaches focus on verifiable evidence citations for rare-disease reasoning [5] or temporal disease information, where ChronoMedKG retrieval improves performance on temporal clinical questions [6]. Results are not uniformly positive: KG grounding helps clinical QA chiefly when the decisive fact is outside the model’s training, rather than for already-known facts [3].","grounded":true}
